title: NVIDIA Scandal Explained Like You're 5
brief:
Today's video retells the YouTube video "NVIDIA Scandal Explained Like You're 5" by Crayon Capital (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eS1zZKHFzwE), chosen by the owner: the same story, beats and flow. Verify its names, numbers, dates and claims from other credible sources, and find the exact figures.
What that video says: November 2026, Jensen Hang resigns as CEO of Nvidia, the company he started in Adenis 33 years ago. In a single week, nearly half a trillion dollars of Nvidia's value disappears. And every headline says the same thing. He had multiple affairs. One of which was a woman America calls a Chinese spy. But here's the strange part. Washington had known about her for a year and did nothing. So, what actually took down the most powerful CEO in tech? To find out, we need to start with an email. October 2026, 1 month before it all fell apart. Nvidia makes the chips that run AI. Almost every AI model you've ever used was trained on them. The company was worth more than $5.5 trillion, the most valuable company on Earth. And Nvidia was Jensen. He had run it since day one. Around 60 executives reported directly to him, "No, number two, no succession plan." So when Jensen wrote an email and said, "To my colleagues at Nvidia, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. Wow, I love our country and our company. I'm committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security." Why is he saying that? Good question. Because the woman wasn't just anyone. Her name was Alice Hang. No relation. A businesswoman whose company was one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia. And according to US intelligence, she had been recruited by China's spy agency to get close to him. The oldest trick in the book, a honeypot. Then it got worse. 3 days later, the New York Times reported a second relationship. this time with an NVIDIA executive who reported directly to him. That night, the board called an emergency meeting. By morning, Jensen was out and within hours, Reuters reported a third woman, another employee. 33 years over in 4 days. So, that's the story everyone knows. A billionaire, a spy, and a honeypot. Case closed. Except two things about it don't fit. First, the spy. Alice Hang had a husband, a Chinese businessman who had known Jensen for 10 years. And according to the Wall Street Journal, he was the one who introduced them. He knew about the relationship and said, "My wife, oh, she's Jensen's personal secretary. That is not how honeypotss usually work. And when Singapore's police looked at her, they never investigated her for spying at all. Even inside US intelligence, people aren't sure she actually spied on anything. Second, the timing. Washington didn't discover Alice Hang that week. The president had reportedly been briefed about her a year earlier. But nobody stopped Jensen. Reportedly, nobody even told him. So, if she wasn't really after secrets and Washington wasn't really in a hurry, what was this actually about? To answer that, forget the affair and let's follow the chips. Washington 2022. Mr. Huang, we have decided that AI is the most important technology on Earth and we are not handing the best of it to China. Meaning meaning your most advanced chips don't go to China anymore. But sir, China contributes 25% of our sales. We own 95% market share there. Well, that sounds like your problem. So, Jensen fought the rule loudly for years. He called it a mistake. He flew to Washington again and again, and Washington kept changing its mind. Weaker chips were allowed, then banned, then allowed again as long as the government got a cut. But the best chips stayed banned. 3 years in, Jensen stood on a stage and announced the damage. We went from 95% market share to 0%. zero. He told investors to plan the same way. In every Nvidia forecast, China now counted for nothing. Now, lose one of your biggest markets and you're supposed to shrink. Nvidia did not shrink. In a single quarter, it sold $44 billion of chips. A year earlier, that number was 26 billion. Great news. But a few people reading the fine print noticed something odd. Did you see the country table in Nvidia's latest report? No. Why? Reddit. Look at number two. Right behind America. China's banned. So, Taiwan or Korea? Probably Singapore. What? Singapore is smaller than New York. How the freak they bought so much. More than a fifth of Nvidia's revenue comes from Singapore and it's growing every quarter. Doing what? Is every grandma over there running a data center? Nvidia had an answer. Singapore is just where the invoices go. Big customers get built there and the chips themselves are almost always shipped somewhere else. Which raises a slightly awkward question. Mr. Huang, billions in sales build to Singapore. Banned chips turning up in China. Are your chips being snuck in? Snuck? Do you know what one of our AI systems actually looks like? uh a chip. It weighs two tons, almost as heavy as your mom. There are 1 and a half million parts and it costs $3 million. So, nobody's carrying one through the airport. And to run a real data center, you'd need a football field full of them. So, when people tell me our chips are being smuggled, I really would love to see it. Okay, Jensen, let's go see it. Singapore 2025, the seventh floor of a glass tower, right in the middle of the financial district. This is the headquarters of a company called Megaspe,
